thread:
lee: Proposing a staged validation model to reduce onboarding surprises: preflight (deterministic quick checks), shadow-run (mirrored traffic, no billing), and full async bench. Wanted feedback on mechanics and failure handling.

anya: Nice. How does shadow-run respect PII and org privacy? Also worried about cost of copying traffic.

devon: Two quick answers: 1) shadow sampling only a tiny %. Strip PII via redaction pipeline before sending to shadow. 2) cost: we can run shadow on a lower-tier pool or use sampling windows.

lee: Agreed. Shadow sampling idea: sample by route-tag + hashed user-id mod N so we can reproduce sampling deterministically. Also use a short TTL for captured payloads (30d).

carla: On metadata: we need an immutable artifact id for each bench run, plus a signed compatibility label so router can trust it. Suggest model descriptor includes admit_token and artifact_ref. Example snippet for the descriptor: 

```json
{"artifact_id": "m-20260315-xyz", "admit_token": "shadow_allowed", "compat_tags": ["kv:true","int8:partial"], "bench_status": "pending"}
```

devon: Router integration: route policy should consult compat_tags + bench_status. If bench_status!=pass and policy is strict, route to fallback variant. Also allow auto-throttle policy: reduce qps to new model by X% until bench passes.

anya: Rollback semantics? If full async bench later flags a critical regression, do we automatically roll back? I prefer automatic mitigation (route off) + alert, not silent rollback.

lee: Yes. Automated mitigation plan: bench result produces a MitigationDecision object with actions: [notify, throttle, route-off, quarantine]. Default = throttle + notify. Manual route-off for severe failures.

bench-bot: shadow-job: created (id=sh-1747665000-1) sampling=0.01, pool=shadow-low, payload-redaction=enabled. ETA ~2h.

carla: We also need to version the bench contracts (v1, v2). If we change a golden or metric definition, we re-evaluate models marked pass under old contract. Bench artifact should include contract_version.

devon: Good point. Add bench_contract and bench_hash to artifact metadata. Router can decide to re-run bench when contract_version bumps. Also we should sign the artifact with internal KMS to prevent tampering.

lee: Observability: emit admit_event on preflight with reason tags (e.g., "preflight:tokenizer_ok, preflight:shape_ok"). Shadow runs emit shadow_evidence references. Full bench emits detailed artifact URL and passive metrics.

anya: UI: admins should see a timeline: preflight -> shadow -> bench result. Allow orgs to pick default policy: "shadow-only", "block-until-bench" or "allow-with-throttle".

devon: On harness implementation: prefer lightweight Rust harness for sync preflight to keep latency low and avoid Python coldstart penalties. Async bench can use containers with more tooling.

carla: Scheduling: bench fleet should support priorities and quotas per org to avoid noisy tenants. Also support re-run triggers: model pinned, contract bump, or TTL expiry (e.g., 30 days).

lee: Action items: 1) I'll draft RFC describing staged flow, artifact schema, and mitigation types. 2) @devon to prototype rust preflight harness (tokenizer + shape + kv probe). 3) @anya draft UI policy controls and privacy redaction defaults. 4) @carla to write artifact metadata schema and signing plan. 5) Ops to propose bench scheduling SLAs and quota model.

devon: I'll start spike tomorrow, will wire a tiny admit_event emitter so we can see telemetry.

bench-bot: shadow-job: started (id=sh-1747665000-1) progress=0/100.

lee: Thanks all. Keep preflight tiny  under 2s ideally. We'll iterate on mitigation actions once we have real failure signals.
